findings: The answer correctly refuses to infer one exact size from five UTF-8 characters per line because the preserved source does not specify the character repertoire or line-ending bytes.

It provides the direct size formula and makes the common 'five CJK characters plus LF gives about 320 MB' interview result conditional on an explicit assumption rather than presenting it as source fact.
The presented Java implementation is complete and calculates actual UTF-8 byte length from a five-code-point sample, avoiding the common String.length()/byte-count confusion.
The deterministic OpenJDK 21 fixture verifies ASCII/LF, common-CJK/LF, four-byte-code-point/LF and ASCII/CRLF byte totals for 20,000,000 lines plus invalid input boundaries.
MB versus MiB, logical length versus allocated disk space, newline amplification and the absence of real filesystem/project facts are explicitly bounded.
